rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can be used both intransitively and transitively; guidance may indicate the road or bring someone to the intended destination.
rows.anchor: “Hüdâ”, hem lâzım ve hem müte‘addî olur. Fâtiha’da beyan olunduğu üzere hidâyet, irâe-i tarîk ve îsâl-i matlûb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the two senses non-conveying guidance and conveying guidance, and says both are used in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: ki birine “hidâyet-i gayr-i mûsile”, diğerine “hidâyet-i mûsile” tâbir olunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As applied to God, guidance can be direction and instruction, or the creation of a person’s guidance and success (tawfiq).
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hakk’a nazaran biri tarîk-i mûsile delâlet u irşad, diğeri halk-ı ihtidâ ve tevfik demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the phrase may suggest enabling success, Elmalılı concludes that Qur’anic guidance here is instruction, since tawfiq and creating guidance are attributes of action, not speech.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’a muzâf olan hidâyetin hidâyet-i irşâdiye olacağı tebeyyün eder. Çünkü tevfik ve halk-ı ihtidâ sıfat-ı kelâma değil sıfat-ı fiile râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification ‘for the God-fearing’ signals that effective guidance and its joining with divine success ordinarily depend on a voluntary human choice.
rows.anchor: insanların bir fi‘l-i ihtiyârîsi ile âdeten meşruttur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an addresses all humanity, but some will not choose its guidance; those whose capacity to respond has been ruined by bad habits may react adversely to it.
rows.anchor: Kur’an herkese tarîk-i hakkı sûret-i umûmiyede göstermek için nâzil olmuş olmakla beraber herkes bunu kabul ve ihtiyarda müsâvî olmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The benefit of the address belongs first to people capable of good choice and taqwa, but taqwa is acquired and so can eventually include all humanity, without ethnic restriction.
rows.anchor: “Arab’a hidâyettir” veya “aceme hidâyettir” denilmiyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittiqa literally means accepting or entering protection; wiqaya is strong safeguarding against things that cause pain or harm.
rows.anchor: “İttikā” vikāyeyi kabul etmek, ta‘bîr-i âharla vikāyeye girmek.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa therefore means taking strong protection and is also used for fear, avoidance, and caution; tevakkī suggests effort, while ittiqa is simpler.
rows.anchor: “Tevakkī”de tekellüf, “ittikā”da sadelik vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s protection is the fullest protection, because human beings cannot control all future outcomes or even all present harms; true taqwa is entering God’s protection.
rows.anchor: En şâmil ve en kuvvetli vikāye ise ancak Allah’ın vikāyesidir. Zira vikāye-i beşer istikbâle ve âkıbete tamamen hâkim olamadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone receives an involuntary, natural share of divine protection, but under divine mercy and voluntary action a person must consciously choose to enter it; its full manifestation depends on concern for the hereafter.
rows.anchor: insanın bu vikāyeye şuur ve ihtiyârıyla girmesi, yani ittikāsı dahi şart olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, taqwa is placing oneself under God’s protection from afterlife harms: avoiding evil and committing to good, with both a positive and a negative aspect joined to fear and love.
rows.anchor: ‘ale’l-ıtlâk “ittikā” veya “takva”: İnsanın kendisini Allah’ın vikāyesine koyarak âhirette zarar ve elem verecek şeylerden iyice koruması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is mistaken to reduce religious taqwa to negative abstinence or mere ascetic restraint.
rows.anchor: takvâ-yı şer‘îyi sırf menfî ve mücerred perhizkârlıktan ibaret zannetmek hatadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Depending on context, the Qur’an also uses taqwa for fear, faith, repentance, obedience, avoiding sin, or sincerity.
rows.anchor: Kur’an’da “ittikā” ve “takva” üç mertebe üzerine zikrolunmuştur ki birincisi azâb-ı muhalledden tevakkī için şirkten teberrî ile iman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first level of taqwa is faith that renounces associating partners with God to escape everlasting punishment, illustrated by 48:26.
rows.anchor: birincisi azâb-ı muhalledden tevakkī için şirkten teberrî ile iman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second, conventional legal level avoids major sins and persistence in minor sins while fulfilling obligations, as in 7:96.
rows.anchor: kebâiri irtikâbdan ve sağāirde ısrardan ictinab ile ferâizi edâ etmektir ki şer‘an müte‘âref olan takva budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest level empties the heart of distractions from God and turns the whole person toward Him; this true taqwa is commanded in 3:102 and has degrees.
rows.anchor: sırr-ı kalbini Hak’tan işgal edecek her şeyden tenezzüh ve bütün mevcûdiyeti ile Hak teâlâ’ya teveccüh ve incizabdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets unite leadership in prophethood and sainthood; worldly duties do not interrupt their spiritual absorption, which is a special divine grace rather than an acquired result.
rows.anchor: nübüvvet ve hem velâyet riyâsetlerini cem‘etmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says 5:93 combines the three levels of taqwa and reports a hadith calling 16:90 comprehensive of taqwa.
rows.anchor: âyetinin de câmi‘u’t-takvâ olduğu bir hadîs-i şerîfte vârid olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic guidance includes every level of taqwa, and ‘the God-fearing’ should be understood broadly as anyone who practices taqwa in any degree.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın hidâyeti bu merâtib-i takvâdan her birine şâmildir ve هُدًى لِلْمُتَّق۪ينَ hepsinden e‘am olan mutlak ittikā mefhûmuyla tefsir olunmak iktizâ eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He raises the apparent circularity: if Qur’anic guidance requires taqwa, while taqwa is itself learned from Qur’anic guidance, the condition seems circular.
rows.anchor: Burada hidâyet-i Kur’ân’ın ittikā ile meşrut olduğu anlaşılıyor. Hâlbuki ittikā da hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan müstefâd olan bir netice olacağına göre meselede bir devir lâzım gelmiyor mu?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial taqwa means a capacity for taqwa: sound-natured people of sound reason who can avoid obstinacy, hypocrisy, and total doubt and are candidates for certainty.
rows.anchor: burada ibtidâen takvâdan murad mebde’-i takvâ, yani kābiliyyet-i takvâdır. Ve “müttakīn” demek inad ve nifaktan, reyb-i küllîden ictinab edebilecek

rows.speaker: مفسرین
rows.claim: The exegetes gloss the initial muttaqin as people approaching or prepared for taqwa (مشارفون للتقوى).
rows.anchor: müfessirîn bunu مُشَارِفُونَ لِلتَّقْوَى diye tefsir ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance also raises a person to higher degrees, so taqwa includes people at earlier levels; Elmalılı calls this ‘generalization by metaphor.’
rows.anchor: Hidâyet ziyâde-i mertebeye de şâmil olduğundan takva, kābiliyyet-i takvâ ile merâtib-i mütekaddime erbâbından e‘amdır ki buna “umûm-i mecaz” tesmiye edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa is a means to salvation, not the ultimate goal; the desired result of guidance is reaching divine blessings safely from wrath and error, which exceeds taqwa itself.
rows.anchor: takva, gāye-i kusvâ değil vesîle-i felâh u sa‘âdettir. Hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan müstefâd olacak netîce-i matlûbe, gazab u dalâlden sâlim olarak ni‘am-i ilâhiyeye vusul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus Qur’anic guidance starts with those capable of taqwa, carries them through its levels, and reaches eternal happiness, so there is no actual circle.
rows.anchor: hidâyet-i Kur’an kābil-i ittikā olan ve henüz dalâlette bulunanlardan başlayarak merâtib-i takvânın hepsinden geçerek sa‘âdet-i ebediyeye kadar varacağından mütâla‘a-i merâtib ile iştirât-ı takvâda emâre-i devr asla melhuz değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is guidance at both the beginning and the end of spiritual progress, so no one at any rank can dispense with it; it addresses ordinary people and elites, worldly life, and eternal aims.
rows.anchor: Kur’an, hem mebde’ ve hem müntehâ itibariyle hidâyettir. Bunun için insan ne kadar yükselirse yükselsin hidâyet-i Kur’an’dan asla müstağnî olamayacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam teaches necessities of worldly life and the acquisition of eternal ends; the Qur’an also supports the unlimited development of advanced civilizations, not only the spiritual needs of primitive people.
rows.anchor: terakki etmiş medeniyetlerin de nâmütenâhî yükselmesi için damân-ı tekâmül olmak üzere nâzil olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Society remains in crisis because humanity has not established a life order grounded in God’s unity or generally attained divine protection and certainty about the hereafter.
rows.anchor: beşeriyyet-i âmme vikāyetullâha girmemiş ve âkıbet ve âhiretine îkān hâsıl edecek mertebe-i ittikāya yükselememiş olduğundan âlemde buhrân-ı ictimâ‘î ber-devam bulunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening presents the Qur’an’s eternal quality, witnessed reality, epistemic and ethical property, and practical purpose in four linked, uncoordinated sentences; it answers al-Fatiha’s ‘guide us’ prayer.
rows.anchor: kemâl-i ittisâl hasebiyle hurûf-ı ‘atf gibi revâbit-i lafziyeden bile müstağnî dört cümle-i mütenâsikadan mürekkeb bir nazm-ı veciz olarak Fâtiha’daki اهدنا duasının cevâbı olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The composition expands from three simple letters to three nouns and three concise clauses, then three verses and stories, continuing with the general address at 2:21; this unfolding exemplifies Qur’anic coherence.
rows.anchor: evvelâ hattan üç harf-i basîtten, lafzan üç ism-i müfrede inkişaf ediyor. Sâniyen, bunların her birine mütenâzır gibi üç cümle-i vecîze inbisat eyliyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in the unseen can mean believing in God’s unseen or believing even in His absence: faith belongs to the heart, not merely the eye.
rows.anchor: O müttakīler ki gayb-i Hakk’a iman ederler, yahut gıyâben dahi iman ederler. Ta‘bîr-i âharla onlar gözle değil kalb ile iman ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not depend on idols, crosses, or current sensory appearances; they pass from sensible signs to intelligible meanings and discern the unseen realities behind them.
rows.anchor: Şâhid ile meşhûdu temyiz ederler, mahsüsâttan ma‘kulâta intikal edebilirler, hudûs ü fenâ içinde gaybdan şuhûda

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many philosophers locate reality in what is unseen or even invisible, naming it the realm of meaning, command, intellect, spirit, or malakut and making it philosophy’s subject.
rows.anchor: birçok hukemâ, hakikati, görülmeyen ve hatta görülemeyen (invisible) kısmında telakkī ederler ve buna âlem-i ma‘nâ, âlem-i emr, âlem-i akl veya âlem-i rûh veya âlem-i melekût derler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern Western philosophy and natural sciences describe sensory qualities as appearances produced when vibrations reach the senses: light, sound, heat, smell, and taste are examples.
rows.anchor: Fünun ve bilhassa fünûn-ı tabî‘iye gösteriyor ki bunların her biri bir tecellîden

rows.speaker: İmam Gazzâlî
rows.claim: Ghazali says sunlight is not an external object traveling from the sun; it is an event created by divine power when the eye faces the sun, disclosed to people of unveiling.
rows.anchor: İmam Gazzâlî İhyâ’sında şöyle tesbit etmiştir: “Nûr-i şems avamın zannettiği gibi güneşten çıkıp bize kadar gelen bir şey’-i hâricî değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account reduces the five sensory channels to appearances of motion and concludes that the causes of what is seen, including historical events and human choices, are unseen.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı râyiha ve tat da esasında birer ihtizaz olup bizim şâmmemiz veya zâikamıza temâsında koku ve tat olarak tecellî ederler. Demek rü’yet ve şuhûd-i hâricîde vâsıta olan bu beş âmilin hepsi hakikatte harekete râci‘dirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account, the sensory world is a shadow or appearance of unseen reality, which can be apprehended by intellect, insight, and the heart rather than outward sight.
rows.anchor: hakikat gayr-i mer’îdir ve nâ-kābil-i rü’yettir. Mer’î olabilen onun tecelliyâtı, hayâli, zılâli, in‘ikâsâtıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Muslim scholars and philosophers hold that God and the angels cannot be seen by eyesight.
rows.anchor: bu noktada yürüyen ve Allah teâlâ’nın ve melâikesinin rü’yet-i basarla görülmesi mümkin olmadığına kāil olan ulemâ ve hukemâ-yı İslâmiye de vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against a view that makes all ultimate reality purely unseen, Ahl al-Sunna holds that God is the source and encompassing of both seen and unseen; He may be seen in the afterlife without direction or place, but never encompassed, and the unseen aspect remains greater.
rows.anchor: bizim ehl-i sünnetin sahih telakkī ve imanımıza göre hakīkat-i ilâhiye gayb-ı mahz değildir, O gayb u şehâdetin merci‘idir, muhît-i küll-i şey’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels and the afterlife are unseen to us yet capable of being witnessed; ghayb means what is not presently seen, not what can never be seen, since the future becomes visible.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın melâikesi de bize gaybdır, âhireti de, fakat onlar da kābil-i şehâdettir. Meselâ umûmiyetle kuvvet görünemez deriz. Hâlbuki görünen de kuvvetten ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is in an evidence-supported, rationally inferable unseen rather than an evidence-free occult; evidence comes from intellect, self, heart, world, and God’s Book, each showing an aspect of what it proves.
rows.anchor: Biz delilsiz olan gayba değil, delîli olan gayb-i ma‘kūle iman ediyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present is a single visible link between unseen past and future; the human observer sees only what passes now, while the movement and strain of the chain reveal its unseen reaches.
rows.anchor: “dünya” nâmını alan hâl-i hâzır, şuhuddan gayba intikal etmiş bulunan o mâzî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a visible present exists, unseen past and future exist all the more necessarily; beyond both ends of sensory phenomena there is also an inward, transcendent reality.
rows.anchor: Âlem-i şehâdet, tabî‘at-i mahsüse bi’l-imkân varsa âlem-i gayb, tabî‘at-i gayr-i mahsüse evleviyetle ve bi’z-zarûre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ultimate reality is God’s power, which moves the chain, establishes the observer, and encompasses and guarantees both the unseen and the seen; those seeking protection therefore believe in the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: İş o zincirde değil, onu salıp tahrik edenle o berzahı kuran, o râsıdı tutan, o deryâları birbirine karıştırmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith contains belief in the origin, the return, and the hidden means between them; knowledge of the visible world is the fourth, outward means, and their unity is expressed by 57:3.
rows.anchor: başlıca üç rüknü ihtivâ eder: Mebde’e iman, me‘âda iman, mebde ü me‘âd beynindeki vesâit-i bâtıneye iman
